#### 1. hereditary spastic paraplegia 63  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.475)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-74217)

**Proposed mechanism:** AMPD1 (HGNC:450) —DISRUPTS→ Purine Metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-5663200); AMPD2 (HGNC:451) —DISRUPTS→ Purine Metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-5663200); Purine Metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-5663200) —DECREASES→ Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP) (CHEBI:15422); Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP) (CHEBI:15422) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324); Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP) (CHEBI:15422) —LEADS_TO→ Spasticity (HP:0001257). Loss-of-function mutations in AMPD1 (causing MONDO:0014220) and AMPD2 (contributing to hereditary spastic paraplegia 63) both disrupt purine metabolism. This disruption leads to decreased ATP levels, which in turn results in the shared phenotypes of muscle weakness and spasticity.

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of pathogenic variants in AMPD1 or AMPD2 with a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in either disease, or evidence that the two genes act through entirely independent downstream pathways not converging on ATP levels, would falsify this hypothesis.

**Why it matters:** Targeting purine metabolism or ATP supplementation could offer a unified therapeutic strategy for both MONDO:0014220 and hereditary spastic paraplegia 63, given their shared mechanistic basis.
